drills.name: Contact-Point Freeze Forehand
drills.ageSkill: Ages 6–12 or adult starters · ITN 9–10 · UTR 1–3
drills.objective: Groove a contact point in front of the lead hip with a stable finish.
drills.setup: Feeder kneels at the service-line T on the same side and drop/toss-feeds soft balls to waist height.
drills.courtLayout: Player at baseline center-right (right-hander); one cone 1 m in front of the lead foot marks ideal contact.
steps: Player starts in ready position, unit-turns on the feeder's "turn" call.
Feeder tosses to waist height in front of the cone.
Player hits through the ball and FREEZES the finish over the opposite shoulder for 2 seconds.
Coach checks contact in front of the cone and balance on the freeze, then next ball.
cues: Turn the shoulders before the ball bounces

mistakes.mistake: Contact beside or behind the hip
mistakes.correction: Move the cone farther forward and toss earlier so the player must step in.
Narrow the feed and ask for a weight shift onto the front foot.

drills.eligibility: Every fed ball that bounces in the hitting zone at waist height is one opportunity.

kpi.attempt: Player completes a full swing at the ball.
kpi.decision: Player sets up so contact happens in front of the cone (not beside or behind the body).
kpi.execution: Ball clears the net and lands in the singles court AND the finish is held balanced for 2 s.

drills.measurement: Per set, tally four numbers on the Session Execution screen: (1) Eligible opportunities — every fed ball that bounces in the hitting zone at waist height is one opportunity. (2) Attempts — player completes a full swing at the ball. (3) Correct decisions — player sets up so contact happens in front of the cone (not beside or behind the body). (4) Successful executions — ball clears the net and lands in the singles court AND the finish is held balanced for 2 s. Tag each miss with an error type (net, long, wide, wrong choice, late). A sound decision that misses still earns decision credit; an attempt outside eligible conditions is logged as an attempt with no decision credit. Volume: 4 sets × 10 balls.
drills.progression: Feeder moves to the opposite baseline and feeds with racquet; then live crosscourt rally.
drills.regression: Drop-feed from beside the player with a foam ball and a mini-net.
drills.safety: Clear loose balls from the hitting zone between sets; feeder stands beside the net post or behind a screen.

drills.name: Rainbow Rope Forehand (Net Clearance)
drills.ageSkill: Ages 6–12 or adult starters · ITN 9–10 · UTR 1–3
drills.objective: Teach safe net clearance with topspin by hitting over a raised rope.
drills.setup: Tie a rope or elastic 1 m above the net tape across the court. Feeder on the opposite service line.
drills.courtLayout: Player at baseline center; target zone = area beyond the service line (deep half of court).
steps: Feeder sends a medium-pace ball to the forehand.
Player swings low-to-high to lift the ball over the rope.
Coach calls "over" or "under" immediately after each ball.
After 8 balls, review: how many went over AND deep?
cues: Brush up the back of the ball
Aim over the rope, not at the net

mistakes.mistake: Ball goes under the rope (flat swing)
mistakes.correction: Start the racquet head below the ball; exaggerate the lift.

mistakes.mistake: Ball sails long over the baseline
mistakes.correction: Keep the arc but close the face slightly; add more brush.

drills.eligibility: Each fed ball landing in the forehand half that the player can reach in two steps.

kpi.decision: Player chooses a low-to-high path aiming over the rope (not a flat drive under it).
kpi.execution: Ball passes above the rope and lands past the service line inside the singles court.

drills.measurement: Per set, tally four numbers on the Session Execution screen: (1) Eligible opportunities — each fed ball landing in the forehand half that the player can reach in two steps. (2) Attempts — player swings at the ball. (3) Correct decisions — player chooses a low-to-high path aiming over the rope (not a flat drive under it). (4) Successful executions — ball passes above the rope and lands past the service line inside the singles court. Tag each miss with an error type (net, long, wide, wrong choice, late). A sound decision that misses still earns decision credit; an attempt outside eligible conditions is logged as an attempt with no decision credit. Volume: 5 sets × 8 balls.
drills.progression: Lower the rope to 0.6 m and require depth past a line 2 m inside the baseline.
drills.regression: Use orange (stage 2) balls and a 3/4 court.
drills.safety: Clear loose balls from the hitting zone between sets; feeder stands beside the net post or behind a screen.

drills.name: Crosscourt Forehand Consistency Ladder
drills.ageSkill: Ages 6–12 or adult starters · ITN 9–10 · UTR 1–3
drills.objective: Build rally tolerance crosscourt with the largest margin of the court.
drills.setup: Both players on the deuce-side diagonal, forehand-to-forehand.
drills.courtLayout: Singles sideline to the center service line, deuce-side half only; a cone at each baseline center marks recovery.
steps: Coach starts the rally with a soft feed crosscourt.
Players rally forehands crosscourt only.
Count consecutive balls; when the ladder rung (5, 10, 15) is reached, move up.
After every ball, recover toward the cone.
cues: Aim through the middle of the diagonal

mistakes.mistake: Aiming at the sideline too early
mistakes.correction: Put a cone 1.5 m inside the sideline as the target.
Require a touch of the recovery cone line before the next shot.

drills.eligibility: Every incoming ball landing inside the crosscourt half.

kpi.attempt: Player returns the ball with a forehand (not running around to backhand or letting it pass).
kpi.decision: Player directs the ball crosscourt with net clearance of at least 1 m (safe choice).
kpi.execution: Ball lands inside the crosscourt half and the rally continues.

drills.measurement: Per set, tally four numbers on the Session Execution screen: (1) Eligible opportunities — every incoming ball landing inside the crosscourt half. (2) Attempts — player returns the ball with a forehand (not running around to backhand or letting it pass). (3) Correct decisions — player directs the ball crosscourt with net clearance of at least 1 m (safe choice). (4) Successful executions — ball lands inside the crosscourt half and the rally continues. Tag each miss with an error type (net, long, wide, wrong choice, late). A sound decision that misses still earns decision credit; an attempt outside eligible conditions is logged as an attempt with no decision credit. Volume: 3 rounds; target 5 → 10 → 15 ball rallies.
drills.progression: Add a depth line: balls must land past the service line to count.
drills.regression: Play from the service line (mini-court) first.
drills.safety: Clear loose balls from the hitting zone between sets; feeder stands beside the net post or behind a screen.

drills.name: Inside-Out Forehand From the Backhand Corner
drills.ageSkill: Ages 10–16 club/junior players · ITN 6–8 · UTR 4–7
drills.objective: Teach the run-around footwork and hip rotation to hit inside-out to the opponent's backhand.
drills.setup: Feeder at opposite baseline center feeds to the player's backhand third.
drills.courtLayout: Target box: 3 m × 3 m in the opponent's ad-side deep corner (for right-handers).
steps: Player starts at baseline center.
Feeder sends a medium-pace ball to the backhand third.
Player takes small adjustment steps around the ball (banana path) to set an open or semi-open stance.
Hit inside-out into the target box and recover to just left of center (ad side) for the next ball.
cues: Move around the ball, not at it

mistakes.mistake: Running straight at the ball and getting jammed
mistakes.correction: Place a cone the player must circle behind before hitting.
Delay the shoulder opening and finish across toward the target.

drills.eligibility: A fed ball in the backhand third that is medium height and pace, giving time to run around (roughly 1.5 s from bounce on the feeder's side).

kpi.attempt: Player runs around and hits a forehand.
kpi.decision: Player runs around only when there is time; on balls feeding too wide/fast, a backhand is the correct choice (coach mixes in 2 such balls per set).
kpi.execution: Ball lands in the target box or within 1 m of it, past the service line.

drills.measurement: Per set, tally four numbers on the Session Execution screen: (1) Eligible opportunities — a fed ball in the backhand third that is medium height and pace, giving time to run around (roughly 1.5 s from bounce on the feeder's side). (2) Attempts — player runs around and hits a forehand. (3) Correct decisions — player runs around only when there is time; on balls feeding too wide/fast, a backhand is the correct choice (coach mixes in 2 such balls per set). (4) Successful executions — ball lands in the target box or within 1 m of it, past the service line. Tag each miss with an error type (net, long, wide, wrong choice, late). A sound decision that misses still earns decision credit; an attempt outside eligible conditions is logged as an attempt with no decision credit. Volume: 4 sets × 8 balls.
drills.progression: Feeder alternates wide/medium balls; player must read and choose forehand or backhand.
drills.regression: Start the player already on the backhand side so less movement is needed.
drills.safety: Clear loose balls from the hitting zone between sets; feeder stands beside the net post or behind a screen.

drills.name: Inside-In Forehand Change of Direction
drills.ageSkill: Ages 13+ national-level juniors / strong club · ITN 3–5 · UTR 8–11
drills.objective: Change direction from an inside-out position to the open court down the line (inside-in) when the ball allows.
drills.setup: Live rally: one player hits only to the other's backhand corner; the working player may finish inside-in.
drills.courtLayout: Working player's target for inside-in: 2 m wide strip along the opponent's deuce sideline past the service line.
steps: Rally starts with a crosscourt backhand exchange (ad diagonal).
Working player runs around backhands to hit inside-out forehands.
When a ball is short (lands inside the service line + 1 m) or slow, change direction inside-in.
Play out the point after the change of direction.
cues: Inside-out is the default, inside-in is the reward
Don't change direction on a deep ball

mistakes.mistake: Changing direction on deep, high balls
mistakes.correction: Coach freezes play and asks where the ball landed; only short/slow balls qualify.
Aim 1 m inside the sideline and keep the hips more closed.

drills.eligibility: An incoming ball that lands inside a line 1 m behind the service line OR arrives below shoulder height with low pace, while the player is set inside the ad-side alley.

kpi.attempt: Player hits inside-in (down the line from the ad side).
kpi.decision: The inside-in was attempted on an eligible ball AND the player was balanced; inside-in off a deep heavy ball is a wrong decision.
kpi.execution: Inside-in lands in the target strip.

drills.measurement: Per set, tally four numbers on the Session Execution screen: (1) Eligible opportunities — an incoming ball that lands inside a line 1 m behind the service line OR arrives below shoulder height with low pace, while the player is set inside the ad-side alley. (2) Attempts — player hits inside-in (down the line from the ad side). (3) Correct decisions — the inside-in was attempted on an eligible ball AND the player was balanced; inside-in off a deep heavy ball is a wrong decision. (4) Successful executions — inside-in lands in the target strip. Tag each miss with an error type (net, long, wide, wrong choice, late). A sound decision that misses still earns decision credit; an attempt outside eligible conditions is logged as an attempt with no decision credit. Volume: 6 rallies of 6+ balls each.
drills.progression: Allow the defender to cover the line once they read it; reward disguise.
drills.regression: Hand-fed: coach feeds 3 balls inside-out then a short ball for the inside-in.
drills.safety: Clear loose balls from the hitting zone between sets; feeder stands beside the net post or behind a screen.

drills.name: Forehand Depth Zones
drills.ageSkill: Ages 10–16 club/junior players · ITN 6–8 · UTR 4–7
drills.objective: Develop rally depth as a default to push the opponent back.
drills.setup: Draw a line (throw-down lines) 2 m inside each baseline across the court.
drills.courtLayout: Deep zone = between the depth line and the baseline. Short zone = everything in front.
steps: Forehand-only rally (both players may run around backhands).
Ball landing in the deep zone scores 1 point to the hitter.
Ball landing short gives the opponent the option to attack.
First to 11.
cues: Aim at the back fence through the net window

mistakes.mistake: Ball lands at service line repeatedly
mistakes.correction: Raise the net target to 1.5 m above the tape.
Keep height but add brush; 70 % pace.

drills.eligibility: Every rally ball the player hits from behind the baseline in a neutral position.

kpi.attempt: Player hits a forehand with height intended for depth (net clearance 1 m+).
kpi.decision: Player chooses depth (height + spin) rather than a flat low-percentage drive in a neutral situation.
kpi.execution: Ball lands in the deep zone.

drills.measurement: Per set, tally four numbers on the Session Execution screen: (1) Eligible opportunities — every rally ball the player hits from behind the baseline in a neutral position. (2) Attempts — player hits a forehand with height intended for depth (net clearance 1 m+). (3) Correct decisions — player chooses depth (height + spin) rather than a flat low-percentage drive in a neutral situation. (4) Successful executions — ball lands in the deep zone. Tag each miss with an error type (net, long, wide, wrong choice, late). A sound decision that misses still earns decision credit; an attempt outside eligible conditions is logged as an attempt with no decision credit. Volume: 4 games to 11 points.
drills.progression: Deep zone shrinks to 1.5 m; shot must also be crosscourt.
drills.regression: Coach feeds every ball; player only aims for depth.
drills.safety: Clear loose balls from the hitting zone between sets; feeder stands beside the net post or behind a screen.

drills.name: Short-Ball Forehand Approach
drills.ageSkill: Ages 10–16 club/junior players · ITN 6–8 · UTR 4–7
drills.objective: Recognize short balls and transition forward with an approach forehand and split at the net.
drills.setup: Feeder mixes deep feeds (rally) and short feeds (inside the service line).
drills.courtLayout: Approach target: deep third, preferably to the opponent's backhand; split-step cone 1 m behind the service line.
steps: Player rallies two deep fed balls from the baseline.
Third feed is short (inside service line) — sometimes deep again as a decoy.
On a short ball, player moves through it, hits an approach to the deep backhand third, then split-steps at the cone.
Feeder sends a volley ball to finish.

mistakes.correction: Count out loud: hit–step–step–split.
Freeze and point to the service line: was it inside?

drills.eligibility: A fed ball that lands inside the service line and bounces below the net height (ball the player can take inside the baseline).

kpi.attempt: Player moves forward and hits an approach forehand.
kpi.decision: Approach only on short balls; staying back on the deep decoy counts as correct non-attempt (logged as no attempt, no penalty).
kpi.execution: Approach lands in the deep third AND the player reaches the split cone before the next feed.

drills.measurement: Per set, tally four numbers on the Session Execution screen: (1) Eligible opportunities — a fed ball that lands inside the service line and bounces below the net height (ball the player can take inside the baseline). (2) Attempts — player moves forward and hits an approach forehand. (3) Correct decisions — approach only on short balls; staying back on the deep decoy counts as correct non-attempt (logged as no attempt, no penalty). (4) Successful executions — approach lands in the deep third AND the player reaches the split cone before the next feed. Tag each miss with an error type (net, long, wide, wrong choice, late). A sound decision that misses still earns decision credit; an attempt outside eligible conditions is logged as an attempt with no decision credit. Volume: 5 sets × 6 balls.
drills.progression: Live: the feeder becomes a defender who can pass.
drills.regression: Every third ball is short (no decoys).
drills.safety: Clear loose balls from the hitting zone between sets; feeder stands beside the net post or behind a screen.

drills.name: Neutral Forehand Down the Line
drills.ageSkill: Ages 13+ national-level juniors / strong club · ITN 3–5 · UTR 8–11
drills.objective: Learn when a neutral forehand can safely change direction down the line.
drills.setup: Crosscourt forehand rally; the working player may go down the line under rules.
drills.courtLayout: Down-the-line target: strip 2 m wide along the opponent's ad sideline, past the service line.
steps: Rally crosscourt (deuce diagonal) for at least 3 shots each.
Working player may go down the line when the incoming ball is at or inside the baseline and below shoulder height.
After the down-the-line, the point is played out on the full court.
Score: down-the-line winner or forced error = 2, unforced error on DTL = −1.
cues: Change direction from inside the court
Hit through the middle of the net (lowest part)

mistakes.mistake: Going down the line from behind the baseline
mistakes.correction: Mark the baseline + 0.5 m; only from inside that line.
Aim 1 m inside the line; keep the follow-through toward target.

drills.eligibility: Incoming crosscourt ball landing inside 1 m of the baseline and at or below shoulder height at contact, with the player balanced inside the court.

kpi.attempt: Player hits forehand down the line.
kpi.decision: DTL attempted on an eligible ball; DTL from deep behind the baseline or off a high heavy ball is not credited.
kpi.execution: Ball lands in the DTL strip.

drills.measurement: Per set, tally four numbers on the Session Execution screen: (1) Eligible opportunities — incoming crosscourt ball landing inside 1 m of the baseline and at or below shoulder height at contact, with the player balanced inside the court. (2) Attempts — player hits forehand down the line. (3) Correct decisions — dTL attempted on an eligible ball; DTL from deep behind the baseline or off a high heavy ball is not credited. (4) Successful executions — ball lands in the DTL strip. Tag each miss with an error type (net, long, wide, wrong choice, late). A sound decision that misses still earns decision credit; an attempt outside eligible conditions is logged as an attempt with no decision credit. Volume: 5 games to 7 points.
drills.progression: Defender may anticipate; working player must disguise with the same preparation.
drills.regression: Coach feeds 3 crosscourt balls then a short-ish ball for DTL.
drills.safety: Clear loose balls from the hitting zone between sets; feeder stands beside the net post or behind a screen.

drills.name: Take-It-on-the-Rise Forehand
drills.ageSkill: Ages 13+ national-level juniors / strong club · ITN 3–5 · UTR 8–11
drills.objective: Take time away by contacting high-bouncing balls on the rise instead of retreating.
drills.setup: Feeder sends heavy topspin balls landing 2–3 m inside the baseline.
drills.courtLayout: Player starts on the baseline; a line 1 m behind the baseline marks "no retreat".
steps: Feeder sends a high, heavy topspin ball.
Player steps in, shortens backswing, contacts the ball before its peak around chest height.
Hit crosscourt deep.
Recover forward to the baseline.
cues: Close the face, ride over it

mistakes.correction: Make the no-retreat line a hard rule; restart if crossed.
Reduce feed height; a compact unit turn.

drills.eligibility: A high-bouncing ball (peak above the shoulder) landing between the service line and 1 m inside the baseline.

kpi.attempt: Player contacts the ball on the rise from on or inside the baseline.
kpi.decision: Player chooses to take it early rather than retreat behind the no-retreat line.
kpi.execution: Ball lands past the service line in the crosscourt half.

drills.measurement: Per set, tally four numbers on the Session Execution screen: (1) Eligible opportunities — a high-bouncing ball (peak above the shoulder) landing between the service line and 1 m inside the baseline. (2) Attempts — player contacts the ball on the rise from on or inside the baseline. (3) Correct decisions — player chooses to take it early rather than retreat behind the no-retreat line. (4) Successful executions — ball lands past the service line in the crosscourt half. Tag each miss with an error type (net, long, wide, wrong choice, late). A sound decision that misses still earns decision credit; an attempt outside eligible conditions is logged as an attempt with no decision credit. Volume: 5 sets × 8 balls.
drills.progression: Live rally where the opponent plays only heavy, high balls.
drills.safety: Clear loose balls from the hitting zone between sets; feeder stands beside the net post or behind a screen.

drills.name: Heavy Topspin Height Window
drills.ageSkill: Ages 10–16 club/junior players · ITN 6–8 · UTR 4–7
drills.objective: Produce heavy topspin with a consistent high net window (1–2 m above the net).
drills.setup: Place two extension poles at each net post with a rope 2 m above the net. Players rally between net tape window (1 m) and the rope.
drills.courtLayout: Full singles court, forehands only; target beyond the service line.
steps: Rally forehands crosscourt.
Ball must pass between 1 m above the tape and the 2 m rope.
Partner calls "window" or "out" aloud for each shot.
Count successful window + depth shots per 3 minutes.

mistakes.correction: Accelerate more vertically; wiper finish.
Lower the hand at the start of the forward swing.

drills.eligibility: Every rally forehand.

kpi.attempt: Player hits a forehand aimed through the window.
kpi.decision: Player selects heavy topspin (rising path, high finish) rather than flat pace.
kpi.execution: Ball passes through the window AND lands past the service line.

drills.measurement: Per set, tally four numbers on the Session Execution screen: (1) Eligible opportunities — every rally forehand. (2) Attempts — player hits a forehand aimed through the window. (3) Correct decisions — player selects heavy topspin (rising path, high finish) rather than flat pace. (4) Successful executions — ball passes through the window AND lands past the service line. Tag each miss with an error type (net, long, wide, wrong choice, late). A sound decision that misses still earns decision credit; an attempt outside eligible conditions is logged as an attempt with no decision credit. Volume: 4 × 3-minute rallies.
drills.progression: Add pace requirement: ball must bounce past the baseline after landing deep (or radar 100+ km/h).
drills.regression: Hand-fed balls with the window only.
drills.safety: Clear loose balls from the hitting zone between sets; feeder stands beside the net post or behind a screen.

drills.name: Short Crosscourt Angle Finish
drills.ageSkill: Ages 13+ national-level juniors / strong club · ITN 3–5 · UTR 8–11
drills.objective: Use the short angle to pull the opponent off the court when the incoming ball is crosscourt and short-ish.
drills.setup: Feeder sends crosscourt balls landing around the service line on the forehand side.
drills.courtLayout: Angle target: box from the singles sideline to 2 m inside, between the net and the service line.
steps: Feeder sends a crosscourt ball.
Player decides: short-and-low ball → angle; deep ball → neutral deep crosscourt.
Hit with extra brush and a shorter finish to land the ball in the angle box.
Recover to cover the down-the-line reply.
cues: Recover to the line after the angle

mistakes.correction: Contact earlier and finish across the body.
Re-state the eligibility line and replay the ball.

drills.eligibility: A crosscourt incoming ball that lands at or inside the service line + 1 m with the player already wide of the singles center.

kpi.decision: Angle is attempted only on eligible balls; deep balls are played back deep crosscourt.
kpi.execution: Ball lands in the angle box.

drills.measurement: Per set, tally four numbers on the Session Execution screen: (1) Eligible opportunities — a crosscourt incoming ball that lands at or inside the service line + 1 m with the player already wide of the singles center. (2) Attempts — player hits the short angle. (3) Correct decisions — angle is attempted only on eligible balls; deep balls are played back deep crosscourt. (4) Successful executions — ball lands in the angle box. Tag each miss with an error type (net, long, wide, wrong choice, late). A sound decision that misses still earns decision credit; an attempt outside eligible conditions is logged as an attempt with no decision credit. Volume: 4 sets × 8 balls.
drills.progression: Live crosscourt rally; first angle earns the point if unreturned.
drills.regression: Hand-feed from the net, player inside the baseline.
drills.safety: Clear loose balls from the hitting zone between sets; feeder stands beside the net post or behind a screen.

drills.name: Run-Around Read Drill
drills.ageSkill: Ages 13+ national-level juniors / strong club · ITN 3–5 · UTR 8–11
drills.objective: Train the decision to run around a backhand only when the ball allows a strong forehand.
drills.setup: Feeder randomly mixes slow/central balls and fast/wide balls into the backhand.
drills.courtLayout: Player starts at baseline center; targets deep ad corner (inside-out) or deep crosscourt backhand.
steps: Feeder sends a random ball to the backhand side.
Player reads speed and width at the opponent's contact.
Slow/central → run around, inside-out forehand. Fast/wide → crosscourt backhand.
Coach confirms the read after each ball.

mistakes.mistake: Running around every ball and getting jammed
mistakes.correction: Coach increases fast/wide feed ratio until the player accepts the backhand.
Call the choice out loud ("fore"/"back") before the bounce.

drills.eligibility: Every ball fed to the backhand half (both runnable and non-runnable balls count).

kpi.attempt: Player commits to a shot choice (forehand run-around or backhand) with a full swing.
kpi.decision: Choice matches the ball: forehand on runnable balls, backhand on fast/wide balls.
kpi.execution: Chosen shot lands deep in its target zone.

drills.measurement: Per set, tally four numbers on the Session Execution screen: (1) Eligible opportunities — every ball fed to the backhand half (both runnable and non-runnable balls count). (2) Attempts — player commits to a shot choice (forehand run-around or backhand) with a full swing. (3) Correct decisions — choice matches the ball: forehand on runnable balls, backhand on fast/wide balls. (4) Successful executions — chosen shot lands deep in its target zone. Tag each miss with an error type (net, long, wide, wrong choice, late). A sound decision that misses still earns decision credit; an attempt outside eligible conditions is logged as an attempt with no decision credit. Volume: 5 sets × 8 balls.
drills.progression: Live point play where the opponent targets the backhand.
drills.regression: Two distinct feed speeds only, announced by color (yellow = slow, green = fast).
drills.safety: Clear loose balls from the hitting zone between sets; feeder stands beside the net post or behind a screen.

drills.name: Open-Stance Wide Forehand & Recovery
drills.ageSkill: Ages 10–16 club/junior players · ITN 6–8 · UTR 4–7
drills.objective: Hit a balanced open-stance forehand when stretched wide and recover with crossover steps.
drills.setup: Feeder sends balls alternately wide forehand and to the center mark.
drills.courtLayout: Cones: wide hitting cone 1 m inside the deuce alley; recovery cone at baseline center.
steps: Player starts at the recovery cone.
Feed wide: player loads the outside leg in open stance and hits crosscourt high and deep.
Push off the outside leg, crossover step, shuffle back to center.
Next ball is fed as the player crosses the center line.

mistakes.mistake: Hitting off the back foot falling away
mistakes.correction: Exaggerate knee bend on the loading leg; ball lower.

mistakes.mistake: Watching the shot instead of recovering
mistakes.correction: Coach feeds next ball earlier.

drills.eligibility: Each wide ball the player can reach with no more than 4 steps.

kpi.attempt: Player reaches the ball and swings from an open stance.
kpi.decision: Player chooses a high crosscourt (neutralizing) ball, not a low down-the-line, when stretched.
kpi.execution: Ball lands deep crosscourt AND the player is back across the center before the next feed.

drills.measurement: Per set, tally four numbers on the Session Execution screen: (1) Eligible opportunities — each wide ball the player can reach with no more than 4 steps. (2) Attempts — player reaches the ball and swings from an open stance. (3) Correct decisions — player chooses a high crosscourt (neutralizing) ball, not a low down-the-line, when stretched. (4) Successful executions — ball lands deep crosscourt AND the player is back across the center before the next feed. Tag each miss with an error type (net, long, wide, wrong choice, late). A sound decision that misses still earns decision credit; an attempt outside eligible conditions is logged as an attempt with no decision credit. Volume: 6 sets × 6 balls.
drills.progression: Feeder alternates wide forehand and wide backhand (figure-8).
drills.regression: Wide feeds only, rest between balls.
drills.safety: Clear loose balls from the hitting zone between sets; feeder stands beside the net post or behind a screen.

drills.name: Low Slice Forehand Pick-Up
drills.ageSkill: Ages 10–16 club/junior players · ITN 6–8 · UTR 4–7
drills.objective: Handle low, skidding slice balls on the forehand with knee bend and lift.
drills.setup: Feeder hits underspin feeds that stay low (below knee height).
drills.courtLayout: Player at the baseline; target past the service line crosscourt.
steps: Feeder slices a low ball to the forehand.
Player lowers the body (not the racquet head) and opens the face slightly.
Lift the ball with topspin and net clearance of at least 0.5 m.
Recover.
cues: Bend the knees, not the back

mistakes.correction: Get lower and open the face slightly at the start of the swing.
Use 60 % pace and focus on clearance.

drills.eligibility: Each slice feed that bounces below knee height in the forehand half.

kpi.attempt: Player plays a topspin forehand (not a block/slice) on the low ball.
kpi.decision: Player chooses a safe crosscourt lift rather than flattening the ball.
kpi.execution: Ball clears the net by 0.5 m+ and lands past the service line.

Decelerate in 3 steps.
Stop with feet wider than the shoulders, hips low.
Hold 2 s, walk back.

Cue "knees over toes".

drills.name: Forward-Backward Short/Deep Coverage

Repeat.

Run through the shot.

drills.objective: Build a reliable second serve and an aggressive second-serve return in live play.
drills.setup: Server gets one serve per point (no first serve).
drills.courtLayout: Full singles court; returner position line marked on the baseline.
steps: Server hits one spin serve per point to a planned target.
Returner steps in to the position line and attacks eligible serves.
Play the full set.
Log double faults, return attacks, and points won by each.

mistakes.correction: Accelerate up; brush faster rather than slowing the arm.
Stand on the marked position line.

drills.eligibility: Each service point.

kpi.decision: Server uses a spin second serve to a planned target; returner attacks medium-pace serves.
kpi.execution: Point is won by the player being measured.

drills.measurement: Per set, tally four numbers on the Session Execution screen: (1) Eligible opportunities — each service point. (2) Attempts — server serves and returner returns. (3) Correct decisions — server uses a spin second serve to a planned target; returner attacks medium-pace serves. (4) Successful executions — point is won by the player being measured. Tag each miss with an error type (net, long, wide, wrong choice, late). A sound decision that misses still earns decision credit; an attempt outside eligible conditions is logged as an attempt with no decision credit. Volume: 1 set to 6.
drills.progression: Double faults count as two points.
drills.regression: Two serves allowed, but both at second-serve pace.
drills.safety: Standard live-ball rules: stop play for stray balls; enforce hydration breaks every 15–20 minutes.
